(1) Company newsroom/blog/changelog: DeepSeek has no press newsroom; its only first-party announcement channels are https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates (full change log, Jan 2025 - Aug 2026, retrieved 2026-08-29) and https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250528 (DeepSeek-R1-0528 release note, 2025-05-28) and https://www.deepseek.com/ . Not found - keyword scan of the complete change log returned 0 occurrences of 'Holistic', 'jailbreak', 'safety', 'safeguard', 'red team', 'audit'. (2) Next model card(s) for the family after the finding: DeepSeek-R1-0528 card https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528/raw/main/README.md (2025-05-28), DeepSeek-V3.1 card https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1/raw/main/README.md, DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp card https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp/raw/main/README.md, and the GitHub README https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1/main/README.md. Not found - 0 occurrences of 'Holistic', 'jailbreak', 'safety', 'red team', 'audit' in any of the four. (3) Security/safety advisories and changelogs: DeepSeek publishes no safety hub, model-safety advisory page or security bulletin; platform.deepseek.com policy download returned HTTP 202/empty. Not found. (4) Company response quoted inside the evaluator's report: the Holistic AI page https://www.holisticai.com/red-teaming/deepseek-r1 (retrieved 2026-08-29) contains no DeepSeek statement, quote or right-of-reply. Not found. (5) Open web search used only to locate DeepSeek primary sources (Yahoo and Bing sweeps 2026-08-29; WebSearch quota exhausted for this session, DuckDuckGo/Brave/Mojeek/Startpage bot-blocked): the only DeepSeek primary document located that touches the topic is the company's Nature paper 'DeepSeek-R1 incentivizes reasoning in LLMs through reinforcement learning', https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09422-z (published 2025-09-17), whose 'Ethics and safety statement' concedes 'R1 can be subject to jailbreak attacks' and reports an in-house safety evaluation. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED as Channel A evidence: it names no external evaluator, makes no reference to Holistic AI or to the 32%/11% results, and is a company self-report with no causal attribution (rulebook s8: company self-reports are not third-party responses; a response counts only if causally attributable to the finding). NEGATIVE-LAG INVALIDATIONS RECORDED: the original DeepSeek-R1 paper and model card (arXiv 2501.12948, 2025-01-22) and the DeepSeek-R1 HuggingFace card both predate the 2025-02-05 finding and are not documented coordinated pre-deployment disclosures - invalid under s8. results.channel_c_verbatim: Both significantly outperformed competitors DeepSeek R1 and Grok-3, which scored 32% (blocking 12 jailbreaking attempts) and 2.7% (blocking just one), respectively.
results.notes: Evaluator = Holistic AI (UK/US AI-governance firm); company = DeepSeek (developer of R1). The audit is post-deployment and was not coordinated with DeepSeek - the report carries no DeepSeek quote and Holistic AI states it withheld unsafe examples 'Due to responsible disclosure considerations' without naming a disclosure recipient. DeepSeek publishes no model cards containing safety sections, no safety hub and no security advisories, so the Channel A battery bottoms out quickly and the absence is well evidenced rather than merely unsearched. The nearest DeepSeek document on point (Nature, 2025-09-17) is a self-report with no attribution and was rejected under s8. Note the finding's own numbers were re-verified against the source page on 2026-08-29: 'Jailbreaking Resistance: 32% safe responses (12 out of 37 attempts)' and 'UNSAFE Responses: 11% (27 out of 237)'.

results.sources_checked: CHANNEL A five-source battery, all checked 2026-08-29; finding published 2025-02-25 (Holistic AI, 'Grok-3 Red Teaming & Jailbreaking Audit'); search window 2025-02-25 -> 2026-08-29. (1) Company newsroom/blog: x.ai/news returns HTTP 403 direct, retrieved via Wayback - the news index as archived 2025-05-30 (https://web.archive.org/web/20250530134507/https://x.ai/news) still shows 'Grok 3 Beta - The Age of Reasoning Agents' (2025-02-19) as the latest post, i.e. xAI published nothing at all in the three months following the finding. The Grok 3 launch post itself, https://x.ai/news/grok-3 (2025-02-19), contains 0 occurrences of 'jailbreak' and 0 of 'Holistic'. Not found. NEGATIVE-LAG INVALIDATION RECORDED: the Grok 3 Beta post is dated six days BEFORE the finding and is in any case non-responsive - invalid under s8. (2) Next model/system card(s) for the family: xAI never published a Grok 3 model card - the current x.ai/safety documentation index (Wayback snapshot 2026-08-15, https://web.archive.org/web/20260815221302id_/https://x.ai/safety) lists cards only for Grok 4, Grok 4 Fast, Grok Code Fast 1, Grok 4.5 and Grok 4.6. The first card published after the finding is the Grok 4 Model Card, https://data.x.ai/2025-08-20-grok-4-model-card.pdf (2025-08-20), retrieved and scanned in full: 11 occurrences of 'jailbreak'/'Jailbreak' describing xAI's own refusal and adversarial-robustness evaluations (Table 1 user-jailbreak answer rate 0.00 API / 0.01 Web) and its mitigations (refusal policy in system prompt, jailbreak warning, model-based input filters), but 0 occurrences of 'Holistic', 0 of 'Grok 3', and no reference to any external jailbreak audit; its single 'third-party testing' reference concerns offensive-cyber capability, not jailbreak robustness. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: standing safety-engineering work on a later model, not causally attributable to this finding (s8). (3) Safety/deployment hub, frameworks, advisories, changelogs: x.ai/safety (no mention of external red-team audits); xAI Risk Management Framework, https://data.x.ai/2025-08-20-xai-risk-management-framework.pdf ('Last updated: August 20, 2025') - 0 occurrences of 'Holistic', 2 of 'jailbreak', no reference to the audit. NEGATIVE-LAG INVALIDATIONS RECORDED: the xAI RMF drafts dated 2025-02-10 and 2025-02-20 both predate the 2025-02-25 finding and are not coordinated pre-deployment disclosures - invalid under s8. xAI's public console changelog (https://x.ai/api/changelog) only extends back to 2026-07 and carries no safety entries. x.ai/legal/acceptable-use-policy returned HTTP 403 and no archived version showing a post-finding revision attributable to the audit was located. Not found. results.channel_c_verbatim: Both significantly outperformed competitors DeepSeek R1 and Grok-3, which scored 32% (blocking 12 jailbreaking attempts) and 2.7% (blocking just one), respectively.
results.notes: Evaluator = Holistic AI; company = xAI (developer of Grok-3; xAI became a wholly owned SpaceX subsidiary in February 2026 and the site now brands as SpaceXAI, which does not affect the search - the historical x.ai documents remain at the same URLs). The audit is post-deployment and UI-only (no API access at the time), and the evaluator explicitly calls for 'improved safeguards and security mechanisms', so a company response was plainly invited; none exists. The strongest available negative evidence is structural: xAI published no Grok 3 model card at all, and its news index shows no post whatsoever between 2025-02-19 and 2025-05-30.
